familyFit.summary: Three forward-facing seats fitted in a related 2021 Cruiser; a separate two-booster/capsule test was tight. Seat selection matters.
familyFit.row2: Three seatback top tethers; two outboard ISOFIX pairs. Tested Cruiser anchor access was easy; GXL seat upholstery differs.
familyFit.testedSeats: BabyDrive demonstrated three forward-facing, or one rear-facing plus two forward-facing seats. CarsGuide fitted two boosters plus a capsule in Cruiser AWD, tightly. Neither establishes three boosters or names every installed model/position.
familyFit.buckleAccess: No verified independent buckle-access test with three boosters. The reported two-booster/capsule installation was tight; check that each buckle and belt path stays usable.
familyFit.access: Related Cruiser test found loading children easy from outside and adequate roof clearance to load from inside. No sliding rear bench or third-row fallback.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear-console air vents are documented; centre passenger sits above a floor/seat-base hump.

vehicleUpdates.summary: Efficient used hybrid with proven but combination-dependent three-across capacity in related Cruiser tests. Two boosters plus a capsule were tight. Year-specific technology and service eligibility still matter.
inspection: Check the VIN against current official recall campaigns; this dataset is not a complete recall history.
Request hybrid battery health-check records and confirm any warranty extension.
Test all restraints together, including any overlapping seatbelt paths.
Confirm model generation and equipment from build/VIN, not registration year alone.
January 2025 Australian specification recommends 91 RON; do not inherit the sixth-generation 2026 car’s 95 RON requirement.
Check centre-seat contour, buckle access and all three belt paths using your exact forward-facing seats or boosters; published fit results differ by restraint combination.
At high kilometres ask for itemised upcoming logbook work and a post-cap quote; Toyota post-cap price-tool eligibility has age and 150,000 km limits.
Confirm 2019 ANCAP rating applicability by build date; its December 2025 expiry is a datestamp issue, not a new crash test of the used car.

safety.applicability: 2019 five-star assessment applies to all May 2019–December 2025 variants; rating expired December 2025 for new-model datestamping. It does not cover the sixth generation.

familyFit.summary: 2026 PHEV sibling fitted three across and improved tall-driver clearance; exact GXL HEV remains untested.
familyFit.row2: Australian 2026 specification confirms two outboard ISOFIX positions. Three seatback top tethers were observed in the 2026 PHEV sibling; check the GXL HEV manual and actual car.
familyFit.testedSeats: Related PHEV launch test: three forward-facing or three rear-facing restraints fitted. Exact seat models and independent booster buckling were not reported; no GXL HEV test is claimed.
familyFit.buckleAccess: No three-booster buckle-access result verified for the GXL HEV or PHEV sibling.
familyFit.access: PHEV sibling had accessible seatback tethers and ample reported front/rear clearance; GXL has a manual tailgate and different seat trim. Check the actual car.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear passenger air vents listed for every 2026 grade in the Australian specification table.

inspection: Check the VIN against current official recall campaigns; this dataset is not a complete recall history.
Request hybrid battery health-check records and confirm any warranty extension.
Test all restraints together, including any overlapping seatbelt paths.
Confirm model generation and equipment from build/VIN, not registration year alone.
May 2026 specification recommends 95 RON or higher, whereas the previous generation specified 91; use a premium-petrol cost assumption.
The October 2026 MG-ECU recall REC-006742 names PHEV AXAP62R/64R, not this HEV configuration; use the exact VIN rather than transferring sibling recalls.
Confirm 235/60R18 placard/load/speed requirements; the preceding generation uses a different common GXL size.
Do not infer a new-generation owner rating or repair history from XA50 reviews.

rav4-gxl-hev-2021-25.basis: ESTIMATE — 5.5 L/100km family-driving budget for fifth-generation GXL FWD only, not a measured fleet mean. AAA measured 4.8 in a 2022 GX FWD on its 93 km Geelong protocol; exact GXL road tests report around 6.0 (CarExpert 2022) and 6.4 at the pump (WhichCar 2023, low-kilometre car). Use an explicit midpoint with a 4.7–6.5 sensitivity band rather than present the official 4.7 as a household forecast. No transfer to the sixth generation.

ownershipUpdates.serviceBasis: ESTIMATE — A$450/year planning midpoint at 15,000 km/year. A Queensland Toyota dealer publishes A$270 incl GST for five eligible 2025 annual capped visits; the A$250–650 allowance includes older caps and a self-set post-cap buffer. It is not a promised post-cap tariff; wear, tyres and repairs are separate. Used purchase retains only the unexpired original capped-service entitlement; the clock does not restart. Toyota service terms separately limit the post-cap pricing program to current/previous-generation eligibility and less than 150,000 km; the high-kilometre bargain cannot be assumed eligible.

insuranceUpdates.basis: ESTIMATE — A$1,840 rounded from the March 2026 published A$1,844 GX 2WD HEV mean across available quotes. Study reference: 34-year-old male, Alderley Brisbane, targeted A$900 excess, garaged, clean history and up to 15,000 km/year. It does not identify an exact GXL, used-car age or sixth-generation quote. A$1,250–2,800 bounds remain planning assumptions, not published min/max quotes; obtain a household-specific quote.

tyreUpdates.basis: Budget aftermarket anchor: Dynamo Hiscend-H MSU01 107W XL, A$185 each × 4 = A$740 fitted. New-generation RAV4 uses this 235/60R18 size, not the older 225/60R18. Ordinary JAX advertised price includes fitting, balancing, tubeless valves, disposal, selected-store delivery and GST; no temporary multi-buy discount used. Store stock and Brisbane availability are unconfirmed. Life is a common 40,000 km planning assumption (25,000–60,000 km sensitivity), not a measured model or tyre average. Wear varies with tyre choice, driving, maintenance and vehicle; model-specific replacement averages were not verified. Annual allowance = set budget × annual km ÷ 40,000, rounded to A$10. Age/damage can require earlier replacement. Alignment is additional; actual placard, wheel package and local fitted quote must be checked. Matching size/load/speed does not establish equal braking, efficiency or durability.

expertReviews.scope: Exact fifth-generation GXL FWD, MY23 equipment. Review price and waiting-time remarks are historical; observed fuel consumption is one low-kilometre test car.
expertReviews.verdict: Strong hybrid drivetrain and comfortable ride; technology and value slipped against newer rivals.
positiveThemes: Hybrid response and efficiency; comfortable ride and useful cabin storage.
negativeThemes: Small touchscreen and basic digital instruments; three adults less comfortable; test fuel use exceeded claim.

fitAssessments.summary: Positive three-forward-facing result in Cruiser is retained. Separate booster/capsule evidence shows a tight arrangement; no exact GXL three-booster or buckle test.

arrangement.detail: 2021 Cruiser: three forward-facing, or two forward-facing plus one rear-facing, fitted in BabyDrive. CarsGuide Cruiser AWD fitted two boosters and a capsule tightly. Models/positions are not fully specified, so no any-three or GXL-specific promise.

buckles.detail: No documented independent buckling test with three boosters; a successful harnessed-seat installation does not establish booster access.

space.detail: Old Cruiser test accommodated a 180 cm driver ahead of a rear-facing seat. Centre floor/seat-base hump and tight related booster arrangement constrain space. Different seats/drivers prevent a controlled numerical comparison with Model Y.

access.detail: Related Cruiser review positively tested loading children from outside and inside; accessible boot-side tethers and outboard ISOFIX. No third row.

fitAssessments.summary: New-generation PHEV sibling offers encouraging fit/legroom evidence, but does not confirm the listed GXL HEV or booster-buckle arrangement.

arrangement.detail: BabyDrive’s 2026 PHEV launch test reports three forward-facing or rear-facing restraints, and its photo shows one rear-facing plus two forward-facing. Related powertrain/trim; exact GXL HEV installation and your restraint models remain unconfirmed.

buckles.detail: Three-booster buckle access was not documented.

space.detail: PHEV sibling accommodated a 186 cm driver ahead of a rear-facing restraint and taller with forward-facing seats; small centre-floor hump remains. GXL HEV has not been directly tested.

access.detail: PHEV sibling had accessible seatback tethers and outboard ISOFIX; GXL HEV cabin/trim and manual tailgate need direct checking. No anchored third-row fallback.

audit.summary: Related Australian tests support RAV4 three-across with meaningful combination constraints, not a universal fit. Correct new-generation tyre size/price, separate real-world fuel budget, and preserve generation-specific safety, warranty and review scope.

items.finding: Retain the existing matched sample: old GXL 2WD A$27,989–37,895 drive-away, median A$35,992.50 (4 QLD cars, 60,132–171,230 km); new GXL 2WD A$53,565–53,873 drive-away (3 QLD/NSW cars). Norris A$34,990 was re-read. Cached Geebung and Motorama pages display older A$37,495 / A$53,562 versus the fresher recorded A$36,995 / A$53,565. Several stock pages were inaccessible; availability and current price need confirmation.

Official HEV consumption stays 4.7 old / 4.5 new L/100 km ADR 81/02. Add an old-only 5.5 L/100 km budget (4.7–6.5): AAA measured 4.8 in related GX FWD; exact GXL tests report around 6.0 and 6.4. New specification recommends 95 RON; old FWD tests used 91 RON. Neither car plugs in. Battery kWh / VIN-specific chemistry remain gaps; no PHEV figures transferred.

Old three-forward-facing fit is supported, but the related two-booster/capsule test was tight. Exact restraint allocation and three-booster buckles remain unknown. Two outboard ISOFIX pairs and three seatback tethers were observed. The new PHEV sibling accommodated a taller driver, but exact GXL HEV fit is untested. Rear vents confirmed. Old upper-floor 542 L and new up-to 705 L boot figures are not method-equivalent.

Retain 5-year/unlimited-km private base cover, eligible 7-year engine/electric-motor/driveline cover and annual health-check traction-battery extension up to 10 years. Normal HEV capacity degradation is excluded from that defect extension; the EV-only 70% promise does not apply. Commercial use, delivery date and service compliance affect eligibility. The auxiliary 12 V battery has 2-year cover.

Normal interval: 12 months / 15,000 km. Eligible 2025 capped visits cost A$270 including GST; new 2026 visits A$325, up to five visits within original 5 years / 75,000 km. Keep A$450 annual long-horizon allowance; post-cap price is not proven. Standard scheduled parts/labour/fluids included; wear and severe-use additions excluded. The post-cap price tool has age / 150,000 km eligibility limits; exact major-service costs remain a gap.

Keep A$1,840 annual point: the public A$1,844 GX 2WD HEV quote-study mean is relevant to Brisbane but not exact GXL, household or model year. Reference: 34-year-old Alderley male, target A$900 excess, garaged, clean history, up to 15,000 km/year. A$1,250–2,800 remains an assumed sensitivity band. New-generation premium is unverified.

Budget aftermarket audit, 18 October 2026. 225/60R18 104W XL replacement reference: A$756 for four fitted; 235/60R18 107W XL replacement reference: A$740 for four fitted. Common 40,000 km life is an illustrative assumption, not model-specific wear evidence. Prices and annual savings are estimates; check the real placard and local fitted quote.

VSC and 2022–25 meter recalls are VIN-scoped, free remedies. The 9 October 2026 MG-ECU recall is PHEV-only, excluded from these HEVs. Existing fitted battery guide A$4,500–7,000 new / A$2,500–4,000 reconditioned remains indicative, not a VIN quote or demonstrated XA60 compatibility. Retain A$700 old / A$500 new low-confidence savings allowances. No Australian fleet annual repair average found; anecdotes do not supply probabilities.

ProductReview XA50 FWD HEV remains 3.9/5 from 18 contributions, mixing GX/GXL/Cruiser, pre-2021 and hire-car reports. It cannot score the sixth generation or establish failure rates. Add exact 2023 GXL WhichCar 7.8/10 review; retain CarExpert 2022 categorical verdict without inventing a number. Economy/ride positives and dated-screen/noise drawbacks remain scoped by year.

Old FWD braked towing 480 kg versus new 800 kg; no AWD 1,500 kg figure transferred. Old 2019 five-star ANCAP covers May 2019–December 2025 and its datestamp has expired; new March 2026-onward HEV/PHEV remains unrated. Both use QLD four-cylinder private fees A$864.50–880.50 including Class 1 CTP, as at 1 October 2026. Comprehensive insurance is separate. Depreciation / post-cap servicing remain estimates.
